linked_heading: D. Quadratic spectrum and the ghost question [partial]
line_text: The two fields h and h + ∂₍μξ_ν₎ describe the same physical geometry in different coordinates; the linearized curvature, which is what matter can feel, is the same for both [T]. This redundancy is the gauge symmetry of linearized gravity, the linearized diffeomorphisms. It does physical work. A symmetric tensor in four dimensions has ten components, the count calc note [#5](../../../notes/geometric-core.md) lists for the graviton ([§D](../../../notes/geometric-core.md#d-quadratic-spectrum-and-the-ghost-question-partial)), but not all of them can be allowed to propagate. If they did, the components with one time index and one space index would carry kinetic energy of the wrong sign, since such components "enter with the wrong sign under any invariant contraction" ([#6 §2](../../../notes/x-classification.md#2-the-gauge-structure-and-the-no-go-d--t), tagged [T — standard]). The gauge symmetry removes them, together with the other unphysical components, and what remains is a massless spin-2 field, the graviton [T].

linked_heading: 2. Model I: a coset sigma model of (H, K)
line_text: - **The action and the order parameter.** Model I's fields are a phase-space metric H and a real structure K on a 1+1-dimensional base. At H = 1 the vacua form a circle K(φ), ρ maps K(φ) to −K(φ), and "O = K₁₁ flips sign under ρ" ([§2](../../papers/reciprocity-toy-models.md#2-model-i-a-coset-sigma-model-of-h-k); [the vacua](coset-model/vacua.md)).

The v1 paper ([#9 §5](../../../notes/broken-born-program-v1.md#5-the-second-graviton-and-its-mass-the-field-equation-problem-solved)) dropped the clause from its statement of the answer, while its assessment counted "the palindrome theorem cancelling the symmetric-bimetric vacuum energy" among "two results that stand on their own regardless of its fate" ([§11](../../../notes/broken-born-program-v1.md#11-assessment)). #11 writes "its wedge vacuum energy zero by identity", in line with the scope it states in [§7.3](../../papers/broken-born-checkpoint-v2.md#73-palindrome-and-the-vacuum-energy-identity-dv) and the novelty downgrade of [§7.4](../../papers/broken-born-checkpoint-v2.md#74-literature-position-updated-by-this-sessions-search--honesty-upgrade), and its [§15](../../papers/broken-born-checkpoint-v2.md#15-assessment) counts "one identity awaiting a novelty verdict".

The nearest documented statements are in #13, which says X "modifies the dual cone only at short range in momentum [D — [§7](../../papers/broken-born-checkpoint-v2.md#7-the-massive-momentum-graviton) of the checkpoint]" ([§1](../../papers/conjugate-special-relativity.md#1-two-causal-cones)) and "dual-geometric effects are Yukawa-cut in momentum [D — checkpoint [§7](../../papers/conjugate-special-relativity.md#7-summary-of-tethers)]" ([§6](../../papers/conjugate-special-relativity.md#6-what-is-shared-what-is-broken-what-is-open)) ([two causal cones](../../conjugate-relativity/two-causal-cones.md)). The checkpoint section it cites says "Yukawa-cut at 1/M_X", of the couplings of ordinary matter ([#11 §7.5](../../papers/broken-born-checkpoint-v2.md#75-spectrum-d)). The wiki follows #11's wording, and the reading in momentum remains chat-only ([conflicts between sources](../../history/documents/source-conflicts.md); see flag 29 in [`review/wiki-build-flags.md`](../../../review/wiki-build-flags.md)).

The program began with the supposition that monopoles live in conjugate space, which would explain why none of ours are seen ([founding suppositions](../../program/founding-suppositions.md)). As an explanation of the null result this is P.R.'s open conjecture [O], conditional on [#11 §11.4](../../papers/broken-born-checkpoint-v2.md#114-the-magnetic-mirror-conjecture-o-pr-v23)'s shared-photon form and a restated P4 ([Conjecture: conjugate monopoles explain the null result](../../electric-magnetic-duality/monopole-explanation.md); flag 62 in [`review/wiki-build-flags.md`](../../../review/wiki-build-flags.md)). The [checkpoint](../../history/documents/checkpoint.md) gives two grounds against it, neither of which kills it ([#11 §11.1](../../papers/broken-born-checkpoint-v2.md#111-the-monopole-audit-revised-d)): "The relevant duality is electric–magnetic (E↔B, g → 1/g), not x↔p; only the shared-photon form of [§11.4](../../papers/broken-born-checkpoint-v2.md#114-the-magnetic-mirror-conjecture-o-pr-v23) contests this ground, and that form needs P4 restated" (the shared-photon form is the version of [P.R.'s magnetic-mirror conjecture](../../electric-magnetic-duality/magnetic-identification.md#shared-photon) in which momentum-polarized partners of our charged particles carry magnetic charge of our own photon); and "The null result is expected under several standard histories, so it lends the explanation no support: inflation after a unification transition dilutes monopoles [T], and without grand unification there are none to dilute, since the Standard Model has no topologically stable monopoles [T]; flag 59 lists further histories (†). Inflation is the standard account, not an observed epoch" (flag 59). This page's physics is the first of those histories. It applies only if a unification transition produced monopoles, inflation followed it and reheating stayed below it (flag 59; [ordering: which relics survive](#ordering-which-relics-survive)). [#11's Appendix A](../../papers/broken-born-checkpoint-v2.md#appendix-a-audit-of-founding-suppositions-pr-with-fates) records the supposition as "**open in both halves**": as explanation, this open conjecture; as [ontology](../../electric-magnetic-duality/conjugate-monopoles.md), "alive and consequence-bearing", "with P.R.'s conjecture that such monopoles are abundant in momentum space" ([App. A item 5](../../papers/broken-born-checkpoint-v2.md#appendix-a-audit-of-founding-suppositions-pr-with-fates)).

linked_heading: 2. Model I: a coset sigma model of (H, K)
line_text: The program's coset toy model ([model I](toy-models/coset-model/_index.md)) shows these objects explicitly ([toy-model note §2](../papers/reciprocity-toy-models.md#2-model-i-a-coset-sigma-model-of-h-k)). Its two fields, on a 1+1-dimensional base, are H, a metric on the phase plane given by a point Z of the [upper half-plane](../phase-space/modular-field/siegel-domain.md), and K, a real structure with K² = 1 that marks which line of the phase plane counts as position ([the order parameter](order-parameter.md)). The symplectic group Sp(2, ℝ) of area-preserving linear maps of the phase plane ([the symplectic form](../phase-space/reciprocity/symplectic-form.md)) acts on both and leaves the action invariant. At H = 1 the vacua are a circle of real structures K(φ), and "The vacuum manifold is the upper half-plane times this circle"; "The stabilizer of (1, K₀) in Sp(2,ℝ) is {±1}" ([toy-model note §2](../papers/reciprocity-toy-models.md#2-model-i-a-coset-sigma-model-of-h-k), whose model-I results are "All checked symbolically"). Every other element of the group moves the vacuum, ρ among them: "ρ acts as Z → −1/Z and K(φ) → K(φ + π) = −K(φ)" ([§2](../papers/reciprocity-toy-models.md#2-model-i-a-coset-sigma-model-of-h-k)). Within the model's full symmetry group, which adds the sign flip K → −K, the vacuum keeps the twisted element ρ∘(K → −K), so the breaking of ρ has physical consequences only once something couples to the sign of K ([the twisted element](twisted-element.md)). The full calculation is on [Model I vacua, the order parameter and the Goldstone spectrum](toy-models/coset-model/vacua.md), and the vacuum manifold's topology and its other descriptions on [topological defects and the vacuum manifold](topological-defects.md#model-i-the-upper-half-plane-times-a-circle).

linked_heading: 8.2 Not the range of the momentum graviton, and a bound on it [D][V][S]
line_text: The question assumes that X is heavy, as #14 and the worklog do. The [checkpoint](../../history/documents/checkpoint.md) fixes no value for X's mass; it gives only M_X ∝ 2(β₁+β₂) ([#11 §7.5](../../papers/broken-born-checkpoint-v2.md#75-spectrum-d); see flag 5 in [`review/wiki-build-flags.md`](../../../review/wiki-build-flags.md)). The [phase-space-diameter note](../../cosmology/scale-factor-duality/phase-space-diameter.md) gives a lower bound, conditional on the program's aligned vacuum, in which the ratio of the two frames' backgrounds is u = 1: torsion balances then require M_X c² > 5.2 meV ([§8.2](../../papers/phase-space-diameter.md#82-not-the-range-of-the-momentum-graviton-and-a-bound-on-it-dvs); tagged [V][S] in its summary, [§9](../../papers/phase-space-diameter.md#9-summary); [the laboratory bound on X's range](../momentum-graviton/range-bound.md)). The note puts that mass against today's expansion rate as "(M_X/H₀)² ≈ 10⁶¹ for the smallest M_X allowed by [§8.2](../../papers/phase-space-diameter.md#82-not-the-range-of-the-momentum-graviton-and-a-bound-on-it-dvs)" ([§6](../../papers/phase-space-diameter.md#6-where-the-rectangle-is-square)), so in the aligned vacuum X lies far above the spin-2 mass of order H₀ that the instability analyses assume. The note also lists the early universe among the bound's caveats: "Bimetric cosmologies are unstable while H exceeds the spin-2 mass" ([Lüben, Mörtsell and Schmidt-May 2020](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.08686) [S]), "so the early universe is a separate question, open in the record" ([§8.2](../../papers/phase-space-diameter.md#82-not-the-range-of-the-momentum-graviton-and-a-bound-on-it-dvs)).

- **Conjugate monopoles.** [`HANDOFF.md` §2](../../../HANDOFF.md#2-scientific-state-one-screen) ties their ontology to the soliton candidate ("As ontology they're alive (the soliton candidate)") and lists their explanation of the null result among its failed claims, "(wrong duality; inflation suffices)". #11 keeps the ontology, with P.R.'s conjecture that they are abundant in momentum space ([§11.1](../../papers/broken-born-checkpoint-v2.md#111-the-monopole-audit-revised-d)), and lists the dark-matter candidacy as open ([§12](../../papers/broken-born-checkpoint-v2.md#12-the-dark-sector-question-three-candidates-and-the-failure-of-one-model)). It lists the explanation as P.R.'s open conjecture [O], in the setting of the shared-photon form, which neither ground kills ([§11.1](../../papers/broken-born-checkpoint-v2.md#111-the-monopole-audit-revised-d), [Appendix A item 5](../../papers/broken-born-checkpoint-v2.md#appendix-a-audit-of-founding-suppositions-pr-with-fates); flag 62). #11 and the root [`CLAUDE.md`](../../../CLAUDE.md) outrank the handoff. → [conjugate monopoles as ontology](../../electric-magnetic-duality/conjugate-monopoles.md); [Conjecture: conjugate monopoles explain the null result](../../electric-magnetic-duality/monopole-explanation.md); [the shared-photon form](../../electric-magnetic-duality/magnetic-identification.md#shared-photon).

linked_heading: 8.1 Not the Born length of the dual special relativity [D][V]

line_text: *The founding suppositions are the eleven ideas P.R. brought to the program at its start. [Appendix A](../papers/broken-born-checkpoint-v2.md#appendix-a-audit-of-founding-suppositions-pr-with-fates) of the [checkpoint](../history/documents/checkpoint.md) ([#11](../papers/broken-born-checkpoint-v2.md)) lists each with the fate the later work gave it: eight are alive in some form and three are open. One became the program's hard core. Others survived in changed form: the conjugate universe became a second description of one state, and the idea that momentum space has its own gravity became a heavy, hidden field. Dark matter as conjugate matter, P.R.'s core conjecture, is alive and covers two of the program's three dark-matter candidates, particles that cluster in space like any other dark matter and magnetic monopoles localized in momentum. One was promoted to a theorem, and one was already established physics. Three are P.R.'s open conjectures: that monopoles in conjugate space explain why none has been found; that the collapse of the conjugate universe powers our accelerating expansion, two versions of which failed; and that dark matter clumps in velocity rather than in space, the founding image, which the program's calculations found required nowhere. Monopoles in conjugate space as objects that exist and a magnetic partner for every electric particle are joined in P.R.'s open [magnetic-mirror conjecture](../electric-magnetic-duality/magnetic-identification.md). In this model the bare μ² is itself renormalized: the level-0 tadpole grows with N, "so fixed bare μ² is not a consistent large-N limit" ([§4](../../../papers/reciprocity-toy-models.md#4-quantum-stability); [the bare mass runs with the truncation](quantum-restoration.md#caveat-1-the-bare-mass-runs-with-the-truncation)). A computation at fixed bare μ² therefore does not settle what happens as N grows. The note lists "the large-N, renormalized fate of the real model's one-loop selection" under "Not shown" ([§6](../../../papers/reciprocity-toy-models.md#6-summary-and-limitations)).

- **Which dual cone.** The cone of [§1](../papers/conjugate-special-relativity.md#1-two-causal-cones) belongs to a 3+1 construction: it lives in (t, p), with time shared between the polarizations and slope c̃. [#13 §6](../papers/conjugate-special-relativity.md#6-what-is-shared-what-is-broken-what-is-open) instead says "our massless dispersion E = c|p| *is* the dual null cone", a cone in (E, p) with slope c that belongs to the four-dimensional Born map, which also exchanges time and energy. [§6](../papers/conjugate-special-relativity.md#6-what-is-shared-what-is-broken-what-is-open) uses that identification to read the bounds that the Fermi Large Area Telescope (Fermi-LAT) places on linear photon dispersion as a test of both cones: they "constrain both cones at once" ([Row 9: no linear photon dispersion](../predictions/photon-dispersion.md#13s-joint-reading)). The v3 worklog records the clash as item O3, raised by P.R., and asks, before any paper claims more, to "fix #13's two cones and settle which construction governs" ([Open: the two dual cones](two-cones-inconsistency.md); [Open: the four-dimensional Born map and dual dynamics](four-dimensional-born-map.md)). The same item notes that a conjugate quantum of zero [invariant length](invariant-length-shell.md) "would sit on the dual null cone with |dp/dt| = c̃", while the withdrawn manuscript [#14](../../notes/knot-dark-matter-standalone.md) described the dark sector in ordinary kinematics: "The papers were never reconciled."

linked_heading: 4. Extent and resolution, and the published answers
line_text: "A region of position extent L resolved to a length ℓ has momentum extent ħ/ℓ resolved to ħ/L: L/ℓ cells of area ħ per axis in either description (L/2πℓ cells of area h)" ([§4](../../papers/phase-space-diameter.md#4-extent-and-resolution-and-the-published-answers)) [T]. With L = c/H₀ = 1.37×10²⁶ m, the Hubble radius of [Friedmann cosmology](friedmann-cosmology.md), and ℓ = l_P = 1.616×10⁻³⁵ m, there are L/l_P = 8.49×10⁶⁰ cells per axis [V]. The box grows with L. Its area is therefore not conserved, unlike the area of the radiation rectangle in [the phase-space diameter relation](phase-space-diameter.md), which stays fixed for a fixed comoving region (§2's table).
